propositions: The §I4a headline 'A child never runs ahead of its parent in the lifecycle' overstates the guarantee provided by the _CASCADING_EDGES enumerated edge table and must be narrowed to document what the table actually guarantees per-edge and same-edge.

The cascade table permits two reachable residuals: closed-to-in-progress child reactivation under an open parent, and blocked-to-in-progress resume under an open parent, neither of which trigger cascading, and both must be explicitly documented as accepted or resolved.

The store-level invariant 'no non-terminal-state ticket can be a child of a closed ticket' is maintained jointly by the two closed-source rows of _CASCADING_EDGES and the unconditional open-children close guard in transition_close.py, not by a total status ordering predicate.

The blocked-to-in-progress resume fires the start-work gate (by design, keying on target status in_progress) but does not cascade because only a blocked parent would be eligible on that same edge, and the gate and cascade answer different questions.

Documentation updates to §I4a, _CASCADING_EDGES comments, and transition.py docstrings must reconcile the gate-vs-cascade disagreement for blocked resume without changing table rows or permission logic (txn.claim_core remains untouched).
